newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica panel approves Johnnic sale terms.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica panel approves Johnnic sale terms.

text.p: A ruling by South Africa's Securities Regulation Panel (SRP) has brought the National Economic Consortium's (NEC) purchase of a stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) one step closer.
The SRP said on Tuesday the NEC would not have to make a comparable offer to Johnnic shareholders should it acquire a stake of 35 percent or more in Johnnic.
The NEC, a grouping of 50 black economic interests, in August struck an agreement with Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd to buy the bulk of its 47.4 percent stake in Johnnic.
The deal was, however, conditional on regulatory assurances that the NEC will not have to make a comparable offer to other Johnnic shareholders should it acquire a stake of 35 percent or more.

In arriving at its ruling, the SRP said it had looked at the fact that there would be no perceived prejudice to Johnnic shareholders by the granting of the ruling because the share prices were ruling continuously in excess of the purchase price payable by the NEC.
It said there had been extensive trading in Johnnic since the publicity around the sale of the stake.
It had also considered that the purchase by the NEC was in the "national economic interest".
The panel said the ruling should not be seen as a precedent.

According to the terms of the Johnnic sale, the NEC will purchase an initial shareholding of at least 20 percent in Johnnic at 50 rand a share and will have an 18-month option to take its stake to 35 percent. A further six percent will be made available via a retail offering by the NEC to smaller NEC members and others within the black community.
